 Illinois man indicted for $66M in fake COVID-19 tests
 A worker at a COVID-19 testing clinic
 Associated Press / Photo by Ted S. Warren 
 Loading the Audio Player... 
 Federal prosecutors in Illinois charged a 52-year-old man with billing the government for $66.2 million in phony COVID-19 tests, according to a Tuesday release from the Department of Justice. A federal grand jury returned a five-count wire fraud indictment against Rajesh “Raj” Patel on Monday. Colin McDonald, the assistant attorney general of the DOJ’s Fraud Division, said Patel allegedly falsified results for hundreds of thousands of COVID-19 tests, exploiting a global crisis for personal gain.
 How did the defendant allegedly carry out the scheme? Court documents named Patel as co-owner and COO of a clinical lab outside Chicago, contracted to run polymerase chain reaction tests, or PCR tests, during the COVID-19 pandemic, according to the DOJ. Patel’s lab allegedly paid Meridian Medical Staffing Inc. to collect biological samples and other information from supposed patients for Patel’s lab to test. Prosecutors allege that between May 2021 and April 2022, Patel returned negative results for at least 380,000 samples without running PCR tests. Prosecutors also believe that many of the supposed patients that Meridian collected samples from either never existed or never gave Meridian specimens for testing. 
 Patel’s lab allegedly billed the federal Health Resources and Services Administration’s Uninsured Program for tests it never ran. HRSA paid the laboratory just over $44 million for fraudulent claims, and Patel personally received about $28 million in proceeds from the scheme, the DOJ said. The DOJ noted that the federal indictment was just an allegation, with all plaintiffs considered innocent until proven guilty in a court of law. Patel could face a sentence of up to 20 years in prison on each count if convicted.
